rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root’s original sense is striking or flogging with a whip or similar implement.
rows.anchor: الأصل في الضرب : الجلد بالسوط وما أشبهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By metaphor, ḍaraba can mean to travel; ḍārib can also mean someone practicing a trade.
rows.anchor: ثم نقل بالاستعارة إلى مواضع فيقال : ضرب في الأرض : إذا سار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍarb can describe a slight-built man; the cited verse calls the speaker a known, quick, keen man.
rows.anchor: والضرب الرجل الخفيف الجسم ، وانشدوا : أنا الرجل الضرب الذي تعرفونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍarb also means a kind or class of things.
rows.anchor: والضرب : الصنف من الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the second radical, al-ḍarab means thick honey.
rows.anchor: والضرب بتحريك الراء : العسل الغليظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḍarība is a tax or other levy imposed on a person.
rows.anchor: والضريبة : ما يضرب على الإنسان من جزية وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḍraba ʿan al-amr means to desist from a matter; ḍarb can also mean a parable.
rows.anchor: وأضرب فلان عن الأمر : كف ، والضرب : المثل

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes give ḍarb the sense of traveling in these verses about setting out in God’s cause or across the land.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضرب في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second Quranic sense is striking with the hand or an implement used by hand.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضرب في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

words: أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة فما فوقها
rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A third sense is describing or setting forth a parable; in 16:74 it means not to describe God by others’ attributes or liken others to Him.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضرب في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: شيخنا
rows.claim: The source’s teacher derives laughter from splitting open, as when the earth opens to bring forth plants.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا رضي الله عنه : الضحك في الأصل : الانشقاق . يقال : ضحكت الأرض

rows.speaker: شيخنا
rows.claim: Laughter names the opening of the mouth in smiling or guffawing; he treats it as distinctive to human beings among animals lacking speech.
rows.anchor: وسمي انفتاح الفم بالتبسم أو القهقهة ضحكا . والضحك : خصيصة من خصائص الإنسان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One definition describes laughter as a natural expansion of the rational soul, showing its response to something delightful.
rows.anchor: وقد حد بعضهم الضحك فقال : انبساط طبيعي يعرض للنفس الناطقة يدل على تأثيرها بلذيذ

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris says al-ḍāḥika is any tooth visible in front of the molars when laughing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : الضاحكة : كل سن يبدو من مقدم الأضراس عند الضحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍaḥūk is a clear road and al-uḍḥūka is something laughed at; ḍaḥka with a still ḥāʾ is someone mocked, while ḍaḥika with a vowel is someone who laughs often.
rows.anchor: والضحوك : الطريق الواضح . والأضحوكة : ما يضحك منه . ورجل ضحكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulūk originally means entering, and it is extended metaphorically where context indicates another sense.
rows.anchor: السلوك : الدخول ويستعار في مواضع تدل عليها القرينة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Exegetes list entering as one Quranic sense of salaka.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أنه في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

words: يسلك من بين يديه ومن خلفه رصدا
rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: They give jaʿala, to place or appoint, as another sense.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أنه في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: They interpret salaka here as imposing a task: making the person climb a steep ascent in Hell.
rows.anchor: والثالث : التكليف . ومنه قوله تعالى في الجن

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A further reported sense is leaving unbelief in the criminals’ hearts.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الترك . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحجر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says God inserts denial into their hearts, making the usage an instance of the first sense, entering.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ندخل التكذيب في قلوبهم فيكون من القسم الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyid originally means one elevated by leadership and rank.
rows.anchor: السيد في الأصل العالي بطريق الرئاسة والرفعة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: One Quranic sense of sayyid is husband, as in the woman’s husband by the door in Joseph’s story.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أنه في القرآن على وجهين

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The second sense is a forbearing or gentle master; the source groups with it the phrase about John in 3:39.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أنه في القرآن على وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Shuyayb’s statement “I see you in prosperity,” al-khayr means low or favorable prices.
rows.anchor: والثاني عشر : رخص الأسعار . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thirteenth sense is righteousness or sound character; another reported interpretation is wealth.
rows.anchor: والثالث عشر : الصلاح . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourteenth sense is strength and capability.
rows.anchor: والرابع عشر : القوة والقدرة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الدخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifteenth sense is worldly wealth or worldly goods.
rows.anchor: والخامس عشر : الدنيا . ومنه قوله تعالى في العاديات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sixteenth sense is reform or moral good.
rows.anchor: والسادس عشر : الاصلاح . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventeenth sense is righteous offspring: God may bring good children from wives one dislikes.
rows.anchor: والسابع عشر : الولد الصالح .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An eighteenth sense is chastity and innocence, as believers should have thought well of one another.
rows.anchor: والثامن عشر : العفة والصيانة . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nineteenth sense is good manners; waiting until the Prophet came out would have been more courteous.
rows.anchor: والتاسع عشر : حسن الأدب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحجرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A twentieth sense is supererogatory acts of worship or other extra good deeds.
rows.anchor: والعشرون : النوافل . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A twenty-first sense is benefit; exegetes explain the verse as gathering provision in a fertile year for a barren year.
rows.anchor: والحادي والعشرون : النافع . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final sense is good in general, the opposite of evil.
rows.anchor: والثاني والعشرون : الخير الذي هو ضد الشر . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalāḥ is a change toward a sound, upright state, and its opposite is corruption.
rows.anchor: الصلاح التغير إلى الاستقامة في الحال . وضده : الفساد

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab says the verb ṣaluḥa is pronounced with fatḥa on its lām.
rows.anchor: وقال ثعلب : يقال صلح الشيء بفتح اللام

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt allows ṣalaḥa and ṣaluḥa, with either fatḥa or ḍamma on the lām.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت : صلح وصلح بفتحها وضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun ṣulūḥ derives from ṣaluḥa; a cited verse asks what goodness remains after one’s parents have been insulted.
rows.anchor: والصلوح مصدر صلح وأنشدوا : -

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Quranic sense is faith, illustrated by the righteous among parents, spouses, and descendants and by the speaker asking to join the righteous.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second sense is high rank; in Joseph’s story, “be righteous” means their standing with their father would improve.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A third sense is gentleness or kind treatment.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A fourth sense is well-proportioned physical creation.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A fifth sense is beneficence: Shuyayb says he seeks reform as far as he can.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A sixth sense is obedience, including the claim “we are reformers” and not spreading corruption after obedience.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A seventh sense is keeping a trust; their father was a man of trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: An eighth sense is dutifulness to one’s parents.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary usage a wakīl is entrusted to manage a matter under agency; the principal must be alive, while a manager for the dead is an executor.
rows.anchor: الوكيل : في العرف من قلد النظر بحكم الوكالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawakkul is displaying one’s incapacity and relying on another; wākl means neglecting one’s affair through reliance, and wakl describes weakness.
rows.anchor: والتوكل : إظهار العجز والاعتماد على الغير ، وواكل فلان

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes give wakīl the sense of guardian or preserver.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الوكيل في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second sense is Lord: God alone is to be taken as wakīl.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الوكيل في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A third sense is controller or one who has authority over another.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الوكيل في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A fourth sense is witness, as in God’s testimony over all things and over an agreement.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الوكيل في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān is exceeding a limit; anyone exceeding his limits in disobedience is a ṭāgh.
rows.anchor: الطغيان : مجاوزة الحد . فكل من جاوز حده في العصيان : طاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb describes a flood bringing a great volume of water, a sea whose waves surge, or blood swelling and flowing.
rows.anchor: وطغى السيل : إذا جاء بماء كثير وطغى البحر : هاجت أمواجه . وطغى الدم : تبيغ

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl recognizes ṭughyān and ṭughwān as variant forms, with both ṭaghaytu and ṭaghawtu as verbs.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل : الطغيان والطغوان لغة . والفعل : طغيت وطغوت

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: One Quranic sense is deviation or error, including the Companion’s denial that he made his associate transgress and the destination prepared for the transgressors.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الطغيان في القرآن على أربعة أوجه . أحدها : الضلال

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Another sense is transgression or overflow, used of the water that rose before the Ark.
rows.anchor: والثاني : العصيان . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحاقة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The fourth listed sense is injustice or oppression in the balance.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الظلم . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One listed referent for al-arḍ is the land of Jordan.
rows.anchor: والرابع عشر : أرض الأردن . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another referent is the land of al-Ḥijr, associated here with the she-camel left to graze in God’s land.
rows.anchor: والخامس عشر : أرض الحجر . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixteenth referent is Persia; another reported interpretation of the land in this verse is women.
rows.anchor: أرض فارس [ ومنه ] ، قوله تعالى في الأحزاب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The seventeenth sense of earth is the heart. Muqātil says the water in the parable is the Quran, so earth denotes hearts.
rows.anchor: والسابع عشر : القلب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الرعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ is what a person obtains to fulfill a purpose or desire; istamtaʿa means obtaining something desired by the self.
rows.anchor: المتاع : اسم لما يحصل به الإنسان مقصودا أو مرادا ، تقول : استمتعت بالشيء إذا حصلت للنفس منه مقصودا

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba gives matāʿ the sense of duration, as in the day extending, and also uses it for useful equipment and benefit, including a divorced woman’s mutʿa.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : والمتاع : المدة

rows.speaker: شيخنا
rows.claim: The teacher defines pilgrimage tamattuʿ as performing ʿumra in the pilgrimage months, then enjoying clothing, perfume, and marital relations before ḥajj.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا رضي الله عنه : ومتعة الحج أن يأتي بالعمرة في أشهر الحج قبل الحج ويفصل بينهما بزمان يستمتع فيه باللباس والطيب والنكاح

rows.speaker: شيخنا
rows.claim: The teacher defines the divorced woman’s mutʿa as what is given when no dower was fixed and the marriage was not consummated.
rows.anchor: ومتعة المرأة ما يدفعه إليها إذا طلقها ولم يكن فرض لها مهرا ولا دخل بها

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: One Quranic sense is provision or respite; Ibn Qutayba reads matāʿ in both cited verses as a period of time.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن المتاع في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second sense is benefit; Ibn Qutayba explains the uninhabited houses as inns that shelter visitors from heat and cold.
rows.anchor: والثاني : المنفعة . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A third sense is metal articles made for use or enjoyment, such as iron, lead, and copper.
rows.anchor: والثالث : ما يتخذ للاستمتاع من حديد ورصاص وصفر ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A fourth sense is the payment or provision for a divorced woman.
rows.anchor: والرابع : متعة المطلقة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The fifth sense is luggage or baggage.
rows.anchor: والخامس : الرحل . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في يوسف ]

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: In ordinary usage najm means a star, perhaps named for its visible appearance; exegetes give the Quranic term this sense in the guidance and stellar references.
rows.anchor: النجم : في مطلق التعارف الكوكب وجمعه نجوم . وقيل : سمي نجما لظهوره

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Najm can mean a plant without a stalk, distinguished from a stalk-bearing tree in the verse about both prostrating.
rows.anchor: والثاني : النبت الذي لا ساق له

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A third sense is portions of the Quran as they were revealed at intervals.
rows.anchor: والثالث : ما كان ينزل من القرآن متفرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, najm can also mean a newly appearing plant, the emerging tip of a horn or tooth, the Pleiades, or any stalkless plant.
rows.anchor: ويقال : النجم : النبت إذا ظهر . ونجم القرن والسن : إذا طلعا . والنجم من النبات : ما ليس له ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāghūt derives from ṭughyān, exceeding bounds; it can denote a disbeliever, sorcerer, idol, Satan, or any rebellious jinn or human.
rows.anchor: الطاغوت : اسم مأخوذ من الطغيان ، والطغيان : مجاوزة الحد . وقد سمي الكافر طاغوتا

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says every object worshipped, whether stone, image, or Satan, is both jibt and ṭāghūt.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : كل معبود من حجر أو صورة أو شيطان ، فهو جبت وطاغوت

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj transmits the same definition from Arabic speakers.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حكى الزجاج عن أهل اللغة

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: One Quranic sense is idols, as in commands to avoid them.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الطاغوت في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second sense is Satan.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الطاغوت في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A third sense identifies al-ṭāghūt with Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf.
rows.anchor: والثالث : كعب بن الأشرف . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaʿām names food; ṭaʿimtu means I tasted, and istaṭʿama al-ḥadīth means asking someone to narrate.
rows.anchor: الطعام : اسم للمأكول . يقال : طعمت الشيء طعما

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that if the imam asks for prompting, the congregation should prompt him by supplying the needed recitation.
rows.anchor: يقول : إذا استفتح فافتحوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeding can apply to anything consumed, including water.
rows.anchor: والإطعام : يقع في كل ما يطعم ، حتى الماء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes Zamzam as food that satisfies and as a cure for illness.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في زمزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāʿim may describe someone in good condition with food; miṭʿām is a frequent host or a heavy eater, and muṭʿam can mean someone provided for. Ṭuʿma is food or livelihood.
rows.anchor: ويقال : رجل طاعم ، أي : حسن الحال في المطعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bow is called muṭʿima because it provides its owner with game; Dhu al-Rumma’s line supplies the poetic usage.
rows.anchor: لأنها تطعم صاحبها الصيد ، قال ذو الرمة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the human addressed in the command to honor parents with Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
rows.anchor: الرابع : سعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some identify the human created in the best form as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra; another view says Hishām ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: والخامس : الوليد بن المغيرة . ومنه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: They identify the ungrateful human in al-ʿĀdiyāt as Qarṭ ibn ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: والسادس : قرط بن عبد الله ومنه قوله

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The human who transgresses after seeing himself as self-sufficient is identified as Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
rows.anchor: والسابع : أبو جهل ابن هشام

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The hasty human who calls for evil as he calls for good is identified as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.
rows.anchor: والثامن ، النضر بن الحارث . ومنه قوله

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: They identify the human whom Satan tells to disbelieve as the worshipper Barṣīṣā.
rows.anchor: والتاسع : برصيصا العابد . [ منه ]

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The human described as ungrateful in al-Ḥajj is identified as Badīl ibn Warqāʾ.
rows.anchor: والعاشر : بديل بن ورقاء . [ ومنه ]

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: They identify the human created anxious in Sūrat Sāʾil as al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq.
rows.anchor: والحادي عشر : الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The human laboring toward his Lord in al-Inshiqāq is identified as al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad.
rows.anchor: والثاني عشر : الأسود بن عبد الأسد

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the human commanded to treat his parents well as ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿa, but the author says the correct occasion is Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
rows.anchor: والثالث عشر : عياش بن أبي ربيعة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The human asked what deceived him about his generous Lord is identified as Kilda ibn Asīd, also called Asīd ibn Kilda.
rows.anchor: والرابع عشر : كلدة بن أسيد ، وقيل أسيد بن كلدة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The human abandoned by Satan is identified as ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.
rows.anchor: والخامس عشر : عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The human told to consider what he was created from is identified as Abū Ṭālib ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
rows.anchor: والسادس عشر : أبو طالب بن عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says rūḥ, rawḥ, and rīḥ share an origin and have closely related meanings differentiated through their vowel patterns.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الروح والروح والريح : من أصل واحد اكتنفته معان تقاربت

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He compares this to related forms for fire/light, inclination, the tongue, and carrying or pregnancy, whose vowel differences distinguish disposition, action, eloquence, blame, language, or what is borne.
rows.anchor: والنار والنور من أصل واحد ، كما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breath used to revive a fire is called rūḥ because it is a wind that comes from the soul; Dhu al-Rumma’s poem uses rūḥ for blowing on the fire.
rows.anchor: ويقال للنفخ [ روح ] لأنه ريح خرج عن الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem’s glossary calls ṭalsāʾ a dirty rag or tinder, says to regulate the breath neither strongly nor weakly, and explains fine and thick kindling.
rows.anchor: والطلساء : خرقة وسخة ، وهي الحراق . والروح : النفخ

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: One Quranic sense is the spirit of living beings, as in the question about the spirit and the creation of Adam.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير [ أن ] الروح في القرآن

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second Quranic sense is Gabriel, called the Holy Spirit, the spirit sent to Mary, the trustworthy spirit, and the spirit descending with the angels.
rows.anchor: والثاني : جبرائيل [ عليه السلام ]

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says karīm means noble or excellent, and can also mean forgiving or beautiful; all senses rest on honor.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الكريم : الشريف الفاضل . ويقال الكريم ويراد به : الصفوح

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The first Quranic sense is excellence or superiority, including God’s honoring Adam’s children and the noble book, messenger, and person.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الكريم في القرآن على ستة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second sense is beauty or goodness, as in a good place, courteous speech to parents, and a beautiful plant variety.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الحسن . ومنه قوله تعالى في النساء

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A third sense is forgiving or generous, as in the references to the gracious Lord.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الصفوح : ومنه قوله تعالى في النمل

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: The fourth sense is abundant; Ibn Qutayba explains the gracious provision as plentiful.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الكثير . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنفال

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A fifth sense is arrogant or self-important, used mockingly in “the mighty, noble one.”
rows.anchor: والخامس : المتكبر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الدخان

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A sixth sense is pious or righteous; the author says it would also be sound to attach this sense to the first category of excellence.
rows.anchor: والسادس : التقي . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle aw can express doubt, as in seeing Zayd or ʿAmr, or choice, as when selecting a coin or its value in silver.
rows.anchor: ' أو ' : حرف يرد للشك . تقول : رأيت زيدا أو عمرا . ويرد للتخيير

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a poetic aw meaning bal, “rather”: the beloved is more pleasing to the eye.
rows.anchor: بدت مثل قرن الشمس في رونق الضحى

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarīr’s verse uses aw in the sense of waw, “and.”
rows.anchor: نال الخلافة أو كانت له قدرا

rows.speaker: توبة
rows.claim: Tawba’s line also uses aw as waw: her sin is upon her as well as her piety.
rows.anchor: وقد زعمت ليلى بأني فاجر

rows.speaker: أبو زكريا
rows.claim: Abū Zakariyyāʾ gives aw a use for deliberate ambiguity, as in “a dinar or more,” and for permission to sit with either al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زكريا : وترد للإبهام ، تقول : اشتريت هذا الثوب بدينار أو أكثر

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes give aw the sense of choice among alternatives, including ransom options and expiatory acts.
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن ' أو ' في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : التخيير

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: A second Quranic use is waw, “and,” including “perhaps he will remember and fear” and “do not obey a sinner or an ingrate.”
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن ' أو ' في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes list a third sense, bal (“rather”), in examples such as “a day or part of a day,” “or nearer,” and “or they increase.”
rows.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن ' أو ' في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba rejects bal as a Quranic sense here: these examples always mean waw, so this chapter reduces to two senses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : وليس هذا الوجه كما تأولوا

rows.speaker: أبو زكريا
rows.claim: Abū Zakariyyāʾ reads “or they increase” as ambiguity for the addressee, neither waw nor bal, since a particle that can retain its literal sense should not be shifted.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زكريا : في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source says ambiguity can sometimes be beneficial, as when God left the answer about the spirit unexplained.
rows.anchor: بل قد تكون المصلحة تارة في الإبهام وتارة في التبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajul is the singular of rijāl, men.
rows.anchor: الرجل : واحد الرجال . وذكر بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the second “man” in the parable is an example set for God, while the first represents believers.
rows.anchor: أحدها : مثال ضربه الله ( عز وجل )

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The man sent to the people or said to announce resurrection is identified as the Prophet Muhammad.
rows.anchor: والثاني : النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The man who brought a warning to Noah’s people is identified as Noah.
rows.anchor: والثالث : نوح عليه السلام . ومنه قوله

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The man who warned ʿĀd is identified as Hūd.
rows.anchor: والرابع : هود . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The man whom Pharaoh’s people consider killing for saying “My Lord is God” is identified as Moses.
rows.anchor: والخامس : موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The two men who urge the Israelites to enter the land are identified as Joshua ibn Nūn and Caleb ibn Yūḥannā.
rows.anchor: والسادس : يوشع بن نون ( وكالب بن يوحنا )

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The believer from Pharaoh’s family, including the man who warns Moses in the city, is identified as Ḥizqīl; another name given is Sharwān.
rows.anchor: والسابع : حزقيل [ مؤمن فرعون

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The man who comes running from the far side of the city in Yā Sīn is identified as Ḥabīb al-Najjār.
rows.anchor: والثامن : حبيب النجار . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The two men of the garden parable are identified as Yemlikha and Fartus, also called Fatrus; Muqātil says Yemlikhia was the believer and Fartus the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: والتاسع : يمليخا وفرطس . وقيل فطرس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil identifies Yemlikhia as the believer and Fartus as the disbeliever in the two-man parable.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : يمليخيا مؤمن وفرطس كافر

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The “great man” from one of the two towns is identified as either Abū Masʿūd al-Thaqafī or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
rows.anchor: والعاشر : أبو مسعود الثقفي أو الوليد بن المغيرة
